I’m not trying to fear monger, but being a bedside nurse is deeply traumatizing. Hospitals operate on profit, not patient care, and it shows. On top of making life or death decisions every shift, we’re constantly penalized for minor, non-clinical tasks like forgetting to update a whiteboard in a patient’s room. Patients, who are understandably frustrated, often don’t realize the impossible position we’re in. You can be running a code trying to save someone’s life while another patient is upset because their call light to use the bathroom wasn’t answered right away. Staffing is chronically unsafe, with burnout and call-outs leaving fewer hands to manage overwhelming patient loads. Many shifts don’t allow for a proper meal or even a bathroom break. It’s 12 straight hours of stress, anxiety, and emotional weight. Nurses are also expected to take on non nursing roles like housekeeping tasks or passing food trays, simply because there’s no support staff. And while those jobs are important, they should not fall to the same person who is simultaneously titrating life-sustaining medications like levophed for critically ill patients. In my trauma ICU, and honestly across every specialty, I don’t know a single nurse who has been in the field for more than five years who still likes their job. That says everything about how broken this system is. At the bedside, the demands are endless, the pressure is crushing, and the support is almost nonexistent. At this point I disassociate because it is a paycheck which I am grateful to have but the entire day before your shift you dread and then the day after a shift it’s almost like you are hungover or beat up because of the emotional toll it takes. I actually started applying to work from home jobs that are literally half of what I make because my quality of life as a bedside nurse ☹
